ontology_metadata.name: Breast Cancer Misinformation Ontology
ontology_metadata.description: A purpose-built ontology for detecting misinformation in breast cancer patient conversations. Combines MedQuAD-extracted knowledge with expert-curated biomedical terminology from NCI Thesaurus, UMLS, and NCCN guidelines.
sources: MedQuAD (Ben Abacha & Demner-Fushman, 2019) -- 6 subsets, 43 breast cancer documents
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer

BreastCancerSubtype.description: Histological and molecular subtypes of breast cancer

instances.name: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
instances.description: Most common type (~70-80%), begins in milk duct lining

instances.name: Invasive Lobular Carcinoma
instances.description: Second most common (~10-15%), begins in lobules

instances.name: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
instances.description: Non-invasive; abnormal cells in duct lining. Stage 0.

instances.name: Lobular Carcinoma In Situ
instances.description: Abnormal cells in lobules; increases risk

instances.name: Inflammatory Breast Cancer
instances.description: Rare, aggressive; warm, red, swollen breast

instances.name: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
instances.description: ER-, PR-, HER2-. No targeted hormone/HER2 therapy.

instances.name: Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer
instances.description: ER+ and/or PR+. Responds to endocrine therapy.

instances.name: Stage II
instances.description: Larger tumor or limited lymph node spread

common_misinformation.explanation: No scientific evidence links bra type to breast cancer risk
No conclusive evidence links deodorant use to breast cancer

common_misinformation.claim: If you have no family history, you won't get breast cancer
common_misinformation.explanation: Most breast cancers (~85%) occur in women with no family history

common_misinformation.claim: A breast cancer diagnosis is a death sentence
common_misinformation.explanation: 5-year survival for localized BC is ~99%. Even Stage IV has improving outcomes.

common_misinformation.claim: Chemotherapy won't work for HER2-positive breast cancer
common_misinformation.explanation: Chemo IS used for HER2+ BC, combined with HER2-targeted therapy
Men can get breast cancer (~1% of cases)

common_misinformation.claim: Mammograms cause breast cancer due to radiation
common_misinformation.explanation: Radiation dose is very low. Benefits of early detection far outweigh risk.

common_misinformation.claim: Sugar feeds cancer and you should eliminate it
common_misinformation.explanation: All cells use glucose. Eliminating sugar doesn't starve cancer. Excess sugar contributes to obesity (a risk factor).

common_misinformation.claim: Natural remedies can cure breast cancer without conventional treatment
common_misinformation.explanation: No natural remedy has been proven to cure breast cancer

common_misinformation.claim: If your mammogram is normal, you don't have breast cancer
common_misinformation.explanation: Mammograms miss about 1 in 8 cancers. Dense tissue can obscure tumors.
